cards.text: Friend, the trick questions are OVER. After Jesus' last answer, nobody dares ask Him anything else (Luke 20:40). So now Jesus asks a question of His own, about the Christ, the Messiah (John 1:41).

cards.question: Jesus asks how it can be said that the Christ is the son of which king?

cards.text: Then Jesus quotes the book of Psalms, where David himself says, 'The Lord said to my Lord.' Two Lords in one line, friend, so read it again SLOWLY.

cards.question: In David's psalm, where does the Lord tell David's Lord to sit?

answers.text: At the head of the table

cards.question: In David's psalm, David's Lord sits there until something happens to His enemies. What is it?

answers.text: They become a footstool for His feet
They run off to a far country

cards.question: Jesus points out that in this psalm, David calls the Christ ___.

cards.text: So Jesus asks, 'So how can He be David's son?' I'm the Papa, friend, and if I ever bowed to little Chip and called him 'Lord,' Mags would announce it to the WHOLE kitchen.
Then, with all the people listening, Jesus turns to His disciples and says, 'Beware of the scribes.' First up: their wardrobe.

cards.question: What does Jesus say the scribes like to walk around in?
Jesus says the scribes love to take the lowest seats at banquets.

cards.text: Not even close: they love the greetings in the marketplaces, the chief seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and these guys can't stand sitting in the second row.

cards.question: Jesus says the scribes defraud widows of their houses, and for a show they make lengthy ___.
Jesus says these scribes will receive a greater reward.

cards.text: Then Jesus looks up and sees the rich putting their gifts into the treasury. Friend, I was bought for one quarter, so watching the rich give makes me feel like pocket change.
And then He sees a poor widow. Jesus just warned about widows losing their houses, friend, so keep your eyes on this one.

cards.question: The poor widow puts two small ___ coins into the treasury.
After watching the gifts go in, Jesus says the poor widow has put in more than all the others.
Two small coins beat all those gifts from the rich? Why does Jesus say the poor widow put in more?

answers.text: She put in all she had to live on
Her two coins were old and very rare
She gave in secret and told no one

cards.question: Jesus says the others gave out of their ___, but she gave out of her ___.

findings.problem: Card 3 already quotes David saying 'The Lord said to my Lord.' That tells the baker that David calls the Christ 'Lord' before card 6 asks them to fill in exactly that word, so card 6 tests nothing.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke 'these guys can't stand sitting in the second row' laughs at the scribes, not with their human situation. Only the first half of the joke, about his years in the drawer, is aimed at himself.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself. Humor about people in Bible stories laughs with their human situation, never at them.

findings.problem: Both right words (surplus, poverty) are about how much someone has. All three wrong words (fear, joy, habit) are feelings or motives. The right pair stands out as the only two words about money, so the baker can pick them without understanding the verse.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
